properties.chose: @ajs, 2026-10-11: "(a) The hub's address is the view." Opening the hub's own design opens its members: the host (flo2) passes _meta["reflow2/view_graph_ids"] — the hub's members filtered by the caller's readable set — on every call to the hub's design; the registry serves that call over a view built from the hub's store and the members'; every id in a reply carries its design (the hub's own unprefixed, members as "<graph_id>:<node id>"); a write resolves the prefix to the owning store and takes that store's lock alone; an edge across designs is a typed link record in the design that makes it. No new address, no new tool. (b) a /v/<view>/mcp address for any set stays considered; (c) a per-session switch and (d) per-call design lists are not chosen (the hosted transport is sessionless per request; (d) touches every schema). properties.decision:
OPEN, 2026-10-11. The requirement (accepted 2026-10-10) says what a view is: N designs the host says the caller may read, open in one process, read through one key space namespaced by graph_id, every ordinary tool running over it, a write landing in the design that owns the node, nothing copied, nothing to release. The resolver #720 built (ReflowService::other_design on _meta["reflow2/readable_graph_ids"]) is the piece a view reuses. What is NOT settled is the door: how a session says "work these designs together", and what a reply's ids look like.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE HUB'S ADDRESS IS THE VIEW'S ADDRESS. A call on the hub's own design (https://api.flo2.io/g/<hub design>/mcp) carries _meta["reflow2/view_graph_ids"] = the hub's members (the host fills it from its hubs table, filtered by the caller's readable set) and the registry serves that call over a ViewGraph built from the hub's store plus the members'. No new URL, no new tool, nothing for a chat to learn: open the hub and the members are there. Ids in replies carry their design ("flo2:req:…", the hub's own unprefixed). Cost: a ViewGraph type implementing the read side of DesignGraph over N stores (search, get_node, scan, edges, the derived scans composed per design), and a write path that resolves the prefix to the owning store and takes that store's write lock alone. MEDIUM-LARGE, mostly in reflow2-core/mcp; flo2's half is one _meta key on calls to a hub's design.
(b) A VIEW ADDRESS OF ITS OWN: /v/<view-id>/mcp, where the host mints a view (a saved set of graph_ids, a hub or any set) and the registry opens it like a design. Cleaner separation (a view is never confused with the hub's own design; "any set the person may read" is served, not only hubs), but a second kind of address to mint, share, revoke and explain, and a chat must be told the view exists.
(c) A PER-SESSION SWITCH: a tool `view_designs {graph_ids}` on any design's session turns that session into a view until `leave_view`. Fits a local stdio client; fits the hosted door badly — the MCP transport flo2 uses is sessionless per request (the 2026-10-02 seat finding), so the switch would have to ride every call anyway, which is (a) with an extra round trip.
(d) PER-CALL: every tool gains `designs: [graph_ids]`. 197 schema changes, a chat choosing on each call; rejected on cost and on the surface-only-grows rule's spirit.

PUSHBACK, KEPT BESIDE IT: (1) ids must be unambiguous in every reply or a chat will write to the wrong design — the prefix is not optional; (2) the view's write path must apply dec:idea-a-relation-between-nodes-in-two-designs-is-recorded-so-linking-works-on-the-one-design (an edge across designs is a typed link record in the design that makes it, never a raw edge between two stores); (3) loop_status, detect_gaps and detect_defects are memoised per design — the view composes their per-design answers and adds the seam checks (compose_and_analyse's), it does not recompute over the union; (4) export/import/release/cut tools are out of a view (they belong to one design); (5) the measurement 1c (open cost of N designs at once on flo2.io) decides whether the view opens members lazily on first touch or all at once. RECOMMENDED: (a), with (b) kept for "any set, not only a hub" later, because the hub is already the one thing shared and the one address a chat opens. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-11 — the hub's address is the view's address (a): a call on a hub's own design carries the hub's member set in _meta, filtered by what the caller may read, and the registry serves it over all of them; ids in replies carry their design. A view address of its own (b) stays considered for arbitrary sets
